transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-04-05
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood), Aisha, Marcus, Elena, Diego (NovaSecure)

Summary (auto):
Weekly POC sync focused on latency tuning. Reviewed TTFT numbers for streaming vs non-streaming, impact of sequence length distribution, and kernel selection/quantization tradeoffs. Agreed next perf runs and data to share.

Topics: TTFT (time-to-first-token), streaming, seq length tails, kernel choices, quantization, KV cache / prefix caching, dedicated vs hosted routing, VPC network checks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll keep this tight, 45 minutes, main goal is TTFT improvements and next perf runs. Aisha?
[00:08] Aisha: yep thanks, quick recap - last week we saw p95 around 260ms for small prompts but TTFT into the app is more like 180-220, it's a bit noisy depending on region.
[00:17] Marcus: and yeah, also seeing worse for longer sessions, abt 2x for 1k tokens session, so seq tail matters.
[00:25] Priya: ok good, so we ran the streaming toggle tests yesterday, initial take is streaming helps perceived latency but increases server-side CPU for small token bursts, and also the model variant selection matters.
[00:35] Diego: quick q - are you using prefix caching for repeated system messages? we have about 40% repeated context across calls.
[00:40] Liam: we did enable KV cache, but I think the pilot config was fallback to cold start for different conversation ids, so might not be warming reliably.
[00:47] Elena: can you, uh, remind me what's the difference between TTFT and first-token after stream starts? cause product team is conflating.
[00:52] Jordan: sure, TTFT here we mean time from request arrival in our edge to first token arriving at the client. streaming-first-token can be different if chunking/flush is used.
[01:02] Aisha: got it. so our target is TTFT < 120ms p95 for the main flow - ideal is <100 but we understand 120 is realistic.
[01:08] Priya: okay, we validated three levers: 1) streaming + smaller chunk size (20-40 tokens) 2) kernel selection - cuBLAS vs custom fused attention kernels (we ran on A100 vs H100 emulation) 3) quantization (int8 vs int4) combined with batching. in our bench, streaming cut perceived latency 25-40% for short prompts but increased overall compute.
[01:28] Marcus: that matches our observation. question - for kernel choices, do you automatically pick fused kernels for e.g. long sequences? we've seen weird slowdowns on 512->1024 seq boundary.
[01:37] Priya: yes so runtime picks kernels based on sequence length distribution; however, sometimes the kernel switch point is blunt and you see a cliff at boundary. we can tune the kernel selection thresholds per GPU class.
[01:46] Diego: is that a config we can change in our private deployment?
[01:49] Priya: yes, on Dedicated/Private you can supply a kernel profile override. we'll provide recommended thresholds.
[01:54] Liam: note - for H100 we prefer the fused attention path but on older Ampere we fall back; that causes the jump you saw.
[02:02] Elena: about quantization - we worry about hallucination/regression in outputs at int4. did you run regression tests?
[02:09] Priya: we ran a small eval suite of 250 prompts and saw <1% semantic regression at int4 on the tuned recipe for this model family, but we should run it on NovaSecure prompts.
[02:18] Jordan: action - Priya to run the quant eval on customer sample set.
[02:22] Aisha: yes we'll share 100-200 representative prompts after this call.
[02:26] Marcus: networking - our p95 egress from app tier to Redwood edge is usually 5-8ms but we have occasional spikes to 30-40ms. could that be the dominant factor?
[02:35] Priya: totally possible. TTFT includes network. we do a breakdown at token level but need end-to-end traces from your side. Diego, can you pull peering logs?
[02:42] Diego: yeah I'll send p95/p99 for last 72h.
[02:45] Jordan: we're going to run kernel-profiled perf with two seq lengths: typical avg 128 and long tail 1024 to catch cliffs; we'll run streaming and non-streaming configs and return a CSV with timing buckets.
[02:56] Elena: question on batching - are you batching at the inference runtime or relying on client-side batching? we don't want extra queuing delay.
[03:03] Priya: runtime batching is workload-aware and aims to keep latency SLOs. for your low-concurrency bursts we recommended micro-batching with tight timeouts (e.g., 3-5ms) so we don't add queuing lag. that plus prefix caching should keep TTFT low.
[03:16] Marcus: if micro-batching uses a timeout, how do you tune it? if we lower timeout we lose batching efficiency and cost goes up.
[03:23] Liam: right - that's a cost/latency tradeoff. we'll produce a recommendation matrix: if you want TTFT p95 <120ms choose timeout 3ms and expect cost +12% on tokens; if you accept 150ms p95 choose 8ms timeout cost +4%.
[03:36] Aisha: ok good. next, there was a note about model fallback. if primary model is busy, do you fallback to a smaller variant? how to preserve semantic parity?
[03:45] Priya: yes we can configure model routing policies with fallbacks. we recommend warm small-critical-model variants and keep a heuristic for confidence-based fallback; we'll share details. for your use case, fallback only on non-critical routes.
[03:55] Diego: any compliance gotchas with KV cache? we need to ensure no customer PII is cached beyond retention policy.
[04:00] Jordan: caching respects per-tenant TTLs and we can disable prefix caching for sensitive endpoints. we'll include config options in the security deck.
[04:07] Elena: cool. can we go over the perf numbers you ran earlier in the week?
[04:11] Priya: sure - quick readout: non-streaming cold start p95 260ms, streaming-first-chunk p95 170-190ms, warmed KV cache streaming p95 120-140ms, int8 quant warmed p95 110-130ms. cliff at 512->1024 where p95 jumps ~80ms on Ampere.
[04:30] Marcus: so best-case warmed + int8 + streaming we're around 110ms p95, which meets target. question is reliability and regression.
[04:38] Priya: agreed. next step is run the same matrix on your exact workload and on Dedicated infra (if you want), and provide a trimmed config.
[04:45] Aisha: budget question - how much more expensive is the Dedicated route to guarantee p95 vs optimizing hosted?
[04:50] Jordan: depends on commits, but generally Dedicated reduces variance and avoids noisy neighbors. we'll re-run cost projection after perf runs; estimate 20-30% higher fixed cost but lower per-token variance and potential savings with optimized kernels.
[04:59] Diego: we'll also want SSO and audit logs turned on for the pilot.
[05:02] Jordan: yes, we'll attach the SOC2 and audit logs doc and how RBAC works.
[05:06] Priya: last little note - we're trying a kernel threshold move in the next run, it should smooth the cliff; if that helps we'll push config to your pilot cluster.
[05:14] Elena: sounds good. thanks everyone.

Recap & Next Steps (verbatim):
- Redwood: run kernel-profiled benchmarks for seq lengths avg128 and 1024, streaming/non-streaming, quantization levels (int8/int4) and share CSVs by 2028-04-09.
- NovaSecure: share 100-200 representative prompts and their frequency distribution by 2028-04-08.
- Priya: run quantization regression on customer prompts and share results by 2028-04-09.
- Diego: provide VPC peering logs and network p95/p99 for last 72h by 2028-04-08.
- Jordan: update pilot pricing after perf runs by 2028-04-10.
